title: Convex Optimization
edition: 1st edition; author PDF seventh printing with corrections, 2009
version: Print publication 2004-03-08; author-hosted corrected 2009 printing; publisher digital record 2013-08-05
pages_equations_tables: Selected author-PDF full-text sections: 4.1.4–4.2.4 pp.136–144, Eq.4.15 and local/global proof; 5.5.2–5.5.3 pp.242–244, Eqs.5.48–5.49; 6.3.1–6.3.2 pp.305–306, Eqs.6.7–6.9. Copyright page read. Other chapters not comprehensively reviewed.
findings: Distinguishes convex guarantees, feasible-point evaluation, optimality conditions and regularized fitting. Nonconvex cases do not inherit global guarantees.
weaknesses_conflicts: No convexity proof for present rolling model. Selected sections only; no whole-book review. Mathematical objective accuracy does not establish physical prediction accuracy.

title: Finite Difference Computing with Exponential Decay Models
edition: 1st edition, Lecture Notes in Computational Science and Engineering 110
version: Publisher eBook 2016-06-10; hardback 2016-06-12. Review anchors use publisher chapter pagination, not longer author draft dated 2016-02-29.
pages_equations_tables: Publisher chapter 2 Analysis, pp.39–58 selected substantive sections 2.1–2.4.2: Eqs.2.1–2.8 amplification/stability; Eqs.2.10–2.14 convergence; model/data error discussion. Publisher frontmatter ISBN/licence read. Author draft consulted for comparison.
findings: Scalar decay shows bounded amplification and monotonicity are different requirements; centered integration can oscillate. Numerical, model and input errors need separate investigation.
weaknesses_conflicts: Scalar constant-coefficient result is not a proof for nonlinear coupled rolling heat exchange. Time substepping alone cannot fix the present spatial strip-midpoint closure. Legacy Python examples require contemporary review.

title: Discrete Inverse Problems: Insight and Algorithms
publisher: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics
edition: 2010 original edition, Fundamentals of Algorithms 7; author errata dated 2015-04-15 consulted
version: SIAM book published 2010; chapter 4 official online record 2012-03-23 independently checked by reviewer; author errata dated 2015-04-15.
pages_equations_tables: Publisher exposed chapter opening extracts are labeled Abstract: chapter 3 (whole chapter pp.23–51), chapter 4 (whole chapter pp.53–83) including Eq.4.1 filtered SVD, chapter 5 (whole chapter pp.85–107). Equation page within chapter not independently verified. Full chapter PDFs unavailable. Author errata consulted. Teaching collection separately identified as R163; slide pages are not book pagination.
findings: Ill-conditioning allows small fit residuals with inaccurate parameters. Spectral regularization trades noise amplification against bias; parameter-choice rules have assumptions and can fail.
weaknesses_conflicts: Book primarily treats linear Fredholm inverse problems with at least as many observations as unknowns. Local sensitivity SVD is not proof of global nonlinear identifiability. Long publisher abstracts/extracts do not establish partial chapter-body access; full chapters not obtained.

title: Short-course teaching materials accompanying Discrete Inverse Problems: Insight and Algorithms
title_note: Descriptive title for the single author-organized short-course collection; component titles are Chapter 1 and 2, Chapter 4, and Chapter 5.
publisher: Technical University of Denmark author website
edition: Undated public teaching collection; reviewed components as served on 2026-10-02
version: Collection date and immutable revision not exposed; do not assign the book publication year to teaching PDFs.
pages_equations_tables: chap12.pdf printed slides 7–11 and 24–29: small-residual ill-conditioning example and singular-value expansion/Picard condition; chap4.pdf slides 11–17: Tikhonov objective, filter factors and augmented least-squares form; chap5.pdf printed slides 5–13: bias/perturbation, discrepancy principle and L-curve. Printed slide numbers used; chapters not fully reviewed.
findings: Author examples distinguish small fit residual from accurate parameters and show regularization bias/noise tradeoffs. Tikhonov can be expressed as augmented least squares.
weaknesses_conflicts: Teaching examples concern mainly linear inverse problems; neither regularization nor a local SVD establishes unique nonlinear rolling parameters. Undated slides and full-book text are separate evidence. Not all course lectures reviewed.
